title: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant C

parts.title: Part 1.1
parts.instructions: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant C - Part 1.1. Level A1-A2. Three short questions about you, your home and your interests, asked one after another. 30 seconds for each answer. No preparation time. Scored items 1-3.

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant C - Part 1.1 (level A1-A2, scored items 1-3).

EXAMINER, read aloud exactly as written:

"Part one. In this part, I am going to ask you three short questions about yourself and your interests. And then, you will see some photos and answer some questions about them. You will have 30 seconds to reply to each question. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime)."

[STAGE DIRECTION: there is no preparation time. Ask the three questions one after another. Allow 30 seconds for each answer and stop the candidate politely when the time is up. Do not help with vocabulary and do not add extra questions.]

QUESTION 1 (30 seconds) - play the chime, then say:
"How do you usually travel to your school or your work in the morning?"

QUESTION 2 (30 seconds) - play the chime, then say:
"Tell me about something you enjoy doing at home in the evening."

QUESTION 3 (30 seconds) - play the chime, then say:
"Who do you talk to most in your family, and what do you usually talk about?"

[STAGE DIRECTION: after question 3 say "Thank you." and move straight on to Part 1.2.]
questions.topic: CEFR Speaking C - Part 1.1 - Home and interests (A1-A2)

parts.title: Part 1.2
parts.instructions: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant C - Part 1.2. Level B1. Two photographs on one theme (everyday shopping) and three questions asked one after another. Question 4 compares the pictures and you have 45 seconds; questions 5 and 6 are opinion questions with 30 seconds each. No preparation time. Scored items 4-6.

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant C - Part 1.2 (level B1, scored items 4-6).

EXAMINER, read aloud exactly as written:

"Now, I am going to ask you to compare two pictures and I will ask you two questions about them. Look at the photographs. What do you see in these pictures?"

[STAGE DIRECTION: show the two photographs together, or read the two descriptions below aloud if no photographs are available. There is no preparation time.]

[PICTURE 1: a busy open-air fruit and vegetable market on a Saturday morning. A seller in an apron is weighing tomatoes on a metal scale while two customers wait beside crates of apples and fresh herbs. Handwritten price cards are propped against the boxes and the stalls have striped awnings.]

[PICTURE 2: a woman standing in the doorway of a flat in the evening, picking up three cardboard delivery boxes that have been left on the floor of the corridor. She is holding her phone with a delivery screen open on it, and there is nobody else in the corridor.]

QUESTION 4 (45 seconds) - this is the compare and describe question; the examiner has just asked it in the sentence above. Play the chime, and if the candidate needs help starting, add:
"Compare the two pictures and say how these two ways of buying everyday things are different."

QUESTION 5 (30 seconds) - play the chime, then say:
"Which of these two ways do you use more often for your own shopping, and why?"

QUESTION 6 (30 seconds) - play the chime, then say:
"Do you think shopping on the internet is a good thing for families in your town? Why, or why not?"

[STAGE DIRECTION: 45 seconds for question 4, then 30 seconds each for questions 5 and 6. Ask them one after another with no preparation time. Then say "Thank you. That is the end of part one." and move on to Part 2.]
questions.topic: CEFR Speaking C - Part 1.2 - Everyday shopping (B1)

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instructions: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant C - Part 2. Level B2. One picture and three questions, all shown at once. You are NOT required to describe the picture. You have 1 minute to think and 2 minutes to answer all three questions together. Scored as item 7.

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant C - Part 2 (level B2, scored as item 7).

EXAMINER, read aloud exactly as written:

"Part two. In this part, I am going to show you a picture and ask you three questions. You will have one minute to think about your answers before you start speaking. You will have two minutes to answer all three questions. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime). Look at the photograph."

[STAGE DIRECTION: show the picture and the three questions together, on one screen or on one card. Then say: "You do not have to describe the picture. It is only there to help you think about the topic."]

[PICTURE: a weekday evening class in a community centre. Eight adults of different ages are sitting at low tables with notebooks and phones in front of them, while a teacher stands at a whiteboard covered in handwriting. Coats hang on the backs of the chairs and the windows behind the class are completely dark.]

THE THREE QUESTIONS (read all three aloud, then give exactly one minute of silent preparation, then play the chime and time two minutes for all three answers together):

1. "Tell me about something useful you have taught yourself, outside school or your job."
2. "How has learning it changed the way you spend your own time?"
3. "In general, what do you think most influences whether adults go on learning new things after they have finished their formal education?"

[STAGE DIRECTION: during the one minute of preparation do not speak and do not answer questions. Start timing the two minutes from the chime. If the candidate stops early, wait five seconds and then say "Is there anything else you would like to add?" once only. Stop the candidate at two minutes, say "Thank you." and move on to Part 3.]
questions.topic: CEFR Speaking C - Part 2 - Learning as an adult (B2)

parts.title: Part 3
parts.instructions:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant C - Part 3. Level C1. One topic statement with a FOR list and an AGAINST list, three points in each. You choose two points from each list and give a balanced argument that represents both sides. You have 1 minute to prepare and 2 minutes to speak. This part is scored as item 8.

EXAMINER NOTE - OFFICIAL SCORING (CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant C):
Eight scored items in total. Items 1-3 (Part 1.1) are scored together 0-5. Items 4-6 (Part 1.2) are scored together 0-5. Item 7 (Part 2) is scored 0-5. Item 8 (Part 3) is scored 0-6. Maximum raw score 21.

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant C - Part 3 (level C1, scored as item 8).

EXAMINER, read aloud exactly as written:

"Part three. In this part, you are going to speak on a topic for two minutes. You can see the topic on the screen and two lists of points - for and against - related to the topic. Choose two items from each list and give a balanced argument to represent both sides of the topic. You have one minute to prepare your argument. You will then have two minutes to speak. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime)."

[STAGE DIRECTION: show the topic and both lists together, or read them aloud clearly, twice if the candidate asks.]

TOPIC STATEMENT:
"City centres should be closed to private cars."

FOR:
1. Cleaner air and quieter streets for the people who live and work there.
2. Space taken back from parking can become pavements, markets and cycle lanes.
3. Fewer cars force a city to build the buses and trams that everyone can use.

AGAINST:
1. Families carrying small children, shopping or tools cannot easily switch to a bus.
2. Small shops in the centre may lose the customers who drive in from outside.
3. Public transport in many cities is not yet reliable enough to replace a car.

[STAGE DIRECTION: remind the candidate once, before the chime, that they must choose two points from each list and argue both sides. Give exactly one minute of silent preparation; the candidate may make notes. Then play the chime and time two minutes. Do not join the discussion. At two minutes say "Thank you. That is the end of the test."]
